facts.statement: Akialoa is an extinct genus of Hawaiian honeycreepers belonging to the subfamily Carduelinae within the family Fringillidae.
facts.quote: Akialoa is an extinct genus of Hawaiian honeycreeper in the subfamily Carduelinae of the family Fringillidae.

facts.statement: All species of Akialoa are extinct and formerly lived throughout the Hawaiian islands.
facts.quote: The ʻakialoa species are all extinct, but they formerly occurred throughout Hawaii.

facts.statement: The Oʻahu, Maui Nui, and Kauaʻi ʻakialoa were once grouped together as a single species known as the greater ʻakialoa.
facts.quote: The Oʻahu ʻakialoa, Maui Nui ʻakialoa, and Kauaʻi ʻakialoa were previously considered a single species, called the greater ʻakialoa.

facts.statement: The Oʻahu ʻakialoa (Akialoa ellisiana) was confirmed extinct in 1837, though an unconfirmed extinction date of 1940 exists.
facts.quote: Oʻahu ʻakialoa, Akialoa ellisiana - extinct, 1837 (confirmed) or 1940 (unconfirmed)

facts.statement: The Maui Nui ʻakialoa (Akialoa lanaiensis) went extinct in 1892.
facts.quote: Maui Nui ʻakialoa, Akialoa lanaiensis - extinct, 1892

facts.statement: The Lesser ʻakialoa (Akialoa obscura) is recorded as extinct in 1940.
The Kauaʻi ʻakialoa (Akialoa stejnegeri) went extinct in 1969.
The Hoopoe-billed ʻakialoa (Akialoa upupirostris) is known to be extinct during the Holocene epoch.
facts.quote: Hoopoe-billed ʻakialoa, Akialoa upupirostris - extinct, Holocene

facts.statement: A Giant ʻakialoa (Akialoa sp.) is recorded as extinct during the Holocene epoch.
facts.quote: Giant ʻakialoa, Akialoa sp. - extinct, Holocene

facts.statement: The genus Akialoa was described by Olson and James in 1995.
Akialoa lived from the Gelasian to the Late Pleistocene, approximately 2.58 to 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Gelasian to Late Pleistocene (2.58 to 0.0117 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The type species of the genus Akialoa is Akialoa obscura.
